defect.snippet: { zone: leg.courier.zone, vehicle: leg.courier.vehicle, courier: leg.courier.id },

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how DeliveryTracker labels and records its delivery metrics? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The delivery_leg_minutes histogram is labeled with courier: leg.courier.id. Courier ids are unbounded, so every courier creates a new series per zone and vehicle, each holding a full set of buckets. As the fleet grows the in-process series map (and the metrics backend) grows without limit, causing memory growth, slow scrapes and high storage cost. Per-courier analysis belongs in logs or the database; the label should be dropped.

choiceQuestions.prompt: repo.save throws while marking an order delivered. What happens to the metrics?
choices: The duration is observed but the result counter is not incremented
Both metrics are recorded because they are computed before the save
Neither metric is recorded and the error propagates
choiceQuestions.explanation: Both observe and inc come after await this.repo.save(leg); a rejection propagates out before either runs. Nothing records a fallback result.

choiceQuestions.prompt: markDelivered is called twice for the same order, sequentially. What does the second call do?
choices: Records a second duration observation with a later deliveredAt
Throws because the loaded leg already has deliveredAt set
Overwrites deliveredAt and increments the counter only
choiceQuestions.explanation: requireOpenLeg throws "already closed" when deliveredAt is defined on the stored leg, so the second sequential call fails before any metric is touched.

choiceQuestions.prompt: How many series does deliveryResults have at most for a single zone?
choices: Four: delivered plus the three failure reasons
choiceQuestions.explanation: deliveryResults uses labels zone and result, where result is "delivered" or one of the three failedReason values, giving four per zone. It never uses order ids.
